evidence.passage: Back in Lake Stevens, he told Vanity Fair: > "I had everyone convinced I'd been off doing this great sales job and making money, and I wasn't..." ... The account is his own, and "everyone" is a storyteller's exaggeration.
evidence.reason: Every quotation verify reopened matches its source in wording and context: GQ, VF, MH, The Independent, Christian Post, Daily Beast, Fox and Wikipedia, plus fresh caption pulls and two fresh transcriptions of the podcast. The two attribution errors from the last round are fixed (MH caveats credited to MH; Mercy named). The prose localizes inference ("by his account", "in Vanity Fair's reconstruction", "The Daily Beast reported", "on this reading") and keeps limits visible (single self-report, father account "his alone"). Not higher: independent testimony is thin (only Gunn), much type evidence is self-report across outlets, podcast quotes rest on machine transcription, and there are small slips (the hook's "Then he added" order; an unlabelled "names worth... more often than pain").

enneagram.passage: The two types part over what the front protects. Where Pratt's record reaches past the demands of the job, it points more often to worth than to pain: - At 19 or 20, sinking into debt, he kept up the story of a successful sales career for the people back home. He hid the outcome, not the depression.
enneagram.reason: The 3-versus-7 test works at the level of motive (what the front protects), and the strongest datum is off camera: he hid the outcome while admitting the depression. Seven gets its full case, including Pratt's own Farley/mask framing and the Maui year, which the article concedes is "the best evidence against it". Nine and Six are tested with sourced discriminators (a purpose clause; 500 vs 17 or 22). Medium confidence is honest. It stops short of higher because the Three case rests heavily on retrospective self-report (a single VF account; a 2026 conversion-narrative "completely deferential"), "value" may be comic rather than market value, and Maui is answered only with a story. The case is supported, not decisive.

originality.reason: The portrait is built from details specific to Pratt: the PMA-equals-OPM chant, 500 cards to 17 or 22, the $35 yearbook, "a great pet fat guy", "Gumper of the year", the bird-hunting "Guardians Ten", and the publicist line he broke for his son. Its through-line (attitude as the product he learned to sell) belongs to this subject. Generic type definitions are brief, and contradictions (Maui, faith, the son) survive the argument.

The front-protects thesis is stated twice (type section and Why-not-7), some paragraphs end on verdict lines, and at 3,926 words it runs past the standard's 3,500 target.
